content:
Apple's fall iPhone lineup this year is rumored to revolve around the iPhone 18 Pro and iPhone Ultra. Here are the three biggest feature differences—apart from price—that could influence your decision to upgrade.

Body design: traditional versus foldable

This difference is the most obvious, but it's worth mentioning because it's also the most significant.

The iPhone 18 Pro and Pro Max will retain the basic body design that iPhones have used for years. Their screen sizes and overall design are reportedly identical to the previous generation. If you love the feel of a traditional iPhone, the iPhone 18 Pro will be your top choice.

As for the iPhone Ultra, it will be Apple's first foldable model. The body design is entirely different, with an outer screen that's shorter and wider than a traditional iPhone, and an inner screen similar to an iPad mini.

Cameras: Pro continues to reign supreme

Apple has always poured its most cutting-edge and innovative camera technology into the Pro series. This year will be no different.

The iPhone Ultra is expected to feature largely the same camera capabilities as the iPhone 18 Pro, but with one major exception: it won't have a telephoto lens.

Sources indicate that the iPhone Ultra's main, ultrawide, and front cameras match those of the Pro series. However, the telephoto lens remains exclusive to the Pro, and is expected to reach new heights this year.

Performance: both pack the A20 Pro chip, but materials affect performance

The iPhone 18 Pro and iPhone Ultra are both expected to use the A20 Pro chip. However, due to differences in design and materials, performance levels may vary.

The iPhone 18 Pro will carry forward the aluminum unibody design from the iPhone 17 Pro, along with the same vapor chamber cooling. These two changes made the iPhone 17 Pro's overall performance better than its predecessor, as the iPhone can stay cooler under heavy workloads.

As for the iPhone Ultra, it will adopt a refined titanium design similar to the iPhone Air. It may also feature a vapor chamber, but so far only one leaker has made that claim. However, due to the different materials, even though the iPhone Ultra packs the same chip as the iPhone 18 Pro, its performance may be slightly lower under scorching sun or when running demanding tasks.
